title: 1972 Portuguese presidential election
summary: The National Assembly returned Américo Tomás unopposed on 25 July 1972 for a third seven-year term that would have run to 1979. It was the last presidential election of the Estado Novo and the only one Salazar had no part in, he having been dead two years. The office had kept one power that mattered — the appointment and dismissal of the head of government — and Tomás had used it in 1968 to put Marcelo Caetano in Salazar's place; his return in 1972 fixed for another seven years the man who would use it again if Caetano moved on the war. It is in the atlas as the last renewal of the regime's own arrangements, twenty-one months before the arrangements ended.

actors.note: the regime filling its own presidency
